description: Multi-dimensional adversarial review of a diff or capability: correctness, security, and spec compliance, with every finding adversarially verified before it is reported.

args.focus: Round 8. Verify the round-7 fixes (commits 8354568, 34a6c58): theme guard invariants (token-name strings, multi-line templates, comment stripping, exact exclusions, file types), lint rule Intl allowlist, container-smoke dirty flag and the .dockerignore/.gitignore mirror test, the Firefox axe slow timeout. Check against the spec delta and design.md. Do NOT re-report what design.md lists under "Accepted limits (review round 3)" or the documented real-compose-stack follow-up; static checks are heuristics backed by e2e, so do not report further obfuscation patterns (eval, string concatenation across variables, encoded strings) as defects; report only defects in shipped behaviour or tests that can pass while the spec is violated by ordinary code.

findings.title: Theme guard's comment stripper treats `/*` inside string literals as a comment opener, hiding real code up to the next `*/`
findings.evidence: `withoutComments` runs `.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, '')` over the raw source with no awareness of strings. Ordinary Vite code such as `import.meta.glob('./pages/*.tsx'); root.classList.add('dark'); /** Routes. */` loses everything from `/*.tsx` to the JSDoc's `*/`, so `'dark'` never reaches QUOTED_SCHEME/TOKEN_WRITE and the scan of real files passes while invariant 3 is broken. The `//` stripper has the same blind spot: it removes the rest of a line when `//` inside a string follows anything other than `:`, a backslash or a quote (for example `'a // dark'` or CSS `url(//cdn…)`).
findings.suggestion: Strip comments with a small tokenizer that skips string, template and regex literals, or use the TypeScript scanner (`ts.createScanner` with skipTrivia) for .ts/.tsx files. Add a `forced` case with a glob string followed by a scheme literal and a later block comment.

findings.title: .dockerignore/.gitignore mirror test compares lines literally, but Docker anchors patterns at the context root while git matches at any depth
findings.evidence: The test only checks that every .gitignore line also appears in .dockerignore. Git matches `*.log`, `.DS_Store`, `uploads/`, `*.dump` and `.env` at any depth, but .dockerignore (Go filepath.Match against the full path) matches them only at the root; only `**/raw/` is depth-independent in both. The Dockerfile does `COPY . .`, so a git-ignored `public/x.dump`, `public/uploads/…` or `src/.env` goes into the build context (and from `public/` into dist), while `git status --porcelain` stays empty and container-smoke records `dirty: false`. That is the claim the test comment says it guarantees ('a clean commit names exactly what the image was built from').
findings.suggestion:
In .dockerignore, prefix the unanchored entries with `**/` (`**/*.log`, `**/.DS_Store`, `**/uploads/`, `**/*.dump`, `**/.env`, `**/.env.*`, …). Make the test normalise patterns: an unanchored gitignore pattern with no slash must appear as `**/

` in .dockerignore. Better still, have container-smoke compare `git ls-files -o -i --exclude-standard` against the paths the image actually received.

findings.title: The .dockerignore mirror test compares pattern strings, but Docker anchors patterns to the context root, so files git ignores in subdirectories still reach the image while the smoke evidence reports a clean commit
findings.evidence: In .gitignore, a pattern like `uploads/`, `storage/`, `backups/`, `*.dump`, `*.log`, `.env`, `.env.*` or `.DS_Store` matches at any depth. In .dockerignore (Go filepath.Match, relative to the context root) the same text matches only at the root. `**/raw/` is the only pattern that is anchored the same way in both. The test only checks that every .gitignore line also appears in .dockerignore, so it passes even though the two files exclude different things. Concrete path: an admin drops a workbook scan into `public/uploads/page1.png` or `public/scan.dump`. Git ignores it, so `git status` is clean and tools/container-smoke.mjs:51 sets dirty=false. The evidence then says the image was built from commit X alone. But `COPY . .` (Dockerfile:9) puts the file in the build context, and Vite copies `public/` into `dist/`, so nginx serves the workbook content to the whole LAN (NFR-4). The round-7 claim in the .dockerignore comment ('the build context is exactly the tracked and untracked files git reports') is false.
findings.suggestion: In .dockerignore, write every unanchored .gitignore pattern as `**/<pattern>` (`**/uploads/`, `**/*.log`, `**/.env`, `**/.env.*`, `**/*.dump`, …). Make the mirror test check meaning rather than text: for each .gitignore pattern without a leading `/`, require either the `**/`-prefixed form or a root-anchored pattern that is provably root-only. Or build from a clean `git archive`/`git worktree` of the commit, and let the smoke count gitignored files under `public/` and `src/` as dirty (`git status --porcelain --ignored`).

findings.title: The theme guard's block-comment stripper starts at `/*` inside an ordinary string literal (e.g. `accept="image/*"`) and deletes all code up to the next `*/`
findings.evidence: `withoutComments` runs `/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g` over the raw source without knowing about strings. `<input type="file" accept="image/*">` (the FR-4 image upload form) and `import.meta.glob('./pages/*.tsx')` are ordinary code, and both contain `/*` in a string. Everything from that `/*` to the next `*/` in the file is erased before the three invariants are checked, for example up to the end of a later JSDoc `/** … */`. A component that has an upload input followed by `root.classList.add('dark')` or `style={{ '--paper': x }}` and then a JSDoc block passes `themeViolations` with no findings. The FR-58 static check is meant to cover the states the e2e cannot reach, such as the dialogs and upload states that later slices add. The round-7 change ('comments are ignored') introduced this false negative, and the fixture list does not test it.
findings.suggestion: Strip comments with a tokenizer that knows about strings: TypeScript's `ts.createScanner` or `@babel/parser` with `tokens: true` for .ts/.tsx/.js, postcss for .css, and an HTML comment pass only for .html/.svg. Or blank out string and template contents only after recording them. Add fine/forced fixtures such as `<input accept="image/*" /> ; el.classList.add('dark'); /** x */` (must be flagged) and `import.meta.glob('./p/*.tsx')`.

findings.title: Theme guard misses ordinary camelCase or underscored scheme class names ('darkMode', 'isDark', 'lightTheme', 'mode_dark')
findings.evidence: Spec (Theme follows the operating system): no app source 'SHALL … name a scheme (`dark`, `light`, `theme…`) in a string literal'. The 'No toggle' scenario: a route with no control is skipped in e2e, and 'the static source check covers it'. Code: QUOTED_SCHEME and TEMPLATE_SCHEME require `\b(dark|light|theme\w*)\b`. In 'darkMode' the 'M' after 'dark' is a word character, so there is no boundary. 'isDark', 'lightTheme', 'appTheme' and 'mode_dark' have no boundary before the scheme word, so none of them match. So `document.documentElement.classList.add('darkMode')` in an effect on a screen with no control, plus `.darkMode { background: … }` in app CSS (no custom property, no scheme API), passes all three invariants. The e2e would skip that screen. These are ordinary class names, not obfuscation. The fixture lists in the test (lines 57-84) only probe word-bounded forms ('dark', 'x dark', `theme-${mode}`), so the test stays green.
findings.suggestion: Match the scheme words at camelCase and underscore boundaries too, for example `(?<![a-z])(dark|light|theme)(?![a-z])` without /i, or `/dark|light|theme/i` applied only inside string literals, with explicit exceptions such as 'highlight'. Add 'darkMode', 'isDark', 'lightTheme' and 'mode_dark' to the `forced` list. Keep identifiers such as `const darkMode` in `fine`.

findings.title: .dockerignore 'mirror' matches .gitignore by string only: Docker anchors patterns at the context root, git does not, so nested git-ignored files (public/uploads/, src/**/*.log, …) reach the image while the smoke reports a clean commit
findings.evidence: The round-7 claim in .dockerignore:13-15 reads: 'the build context is exactly the tracked and untracked files git reports: smoke evidence that names a clean commit really did build from that commit.' The test only checks `patterns('.gitignore').filter(p => !docker.has(p))` is empty, which is string equality. In .gitignore, `uploads/`, `storage/`, `pgdata/`, `backups/`, `*.log`, `*.dump`, `.DS_Store`, `.idea/` and `.vscode/` match at any depth. In .dockerignore (Go filepath.Match against paths relative to the context root) they match only at the root. Only `**/raw/` has the same meaning in both. The Dockerfile does `COPY . .`, and Vite copies `public/` verbatim into dist, which nginx serves. So a git-ignored `public/uploads/page.pdf` (workbook content, NFR-4) or `public/backups/x.dump` is shipped in the image while `git status --porcelain` stays empty and container-smoke-latest.md records dirty=false.
findings.suggestion: Write the unanchored .gitignore patterns as `**/uploads/`, `**/*.log`, `**/*.dump`, `**/.DS_Store` and so on in .dockerignore. Make the test compare semantics, not strings: for each .gitignore pattern without a leading '/' or inner '/', require the `**/`-prefixed form in .dockerignore. Better still, have the test list the actual build context (for example by walking the tree with the .dockerignore rules) and check it against `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard`.

findings.title: Scheme-word invariant misses ordinary camelCase class names ('darkMode', 'isLight', 'appDark')
findings.evidence: QUOTED_SCHEME and TEMPLATE_SCHEME need a word boundary on both sides: `\b(dark|light|theme\w*)\b`. In 'darkMode', 'isLight' or 'appDark' there is no boundary between the scheme word and the next or previous letter, so `root.classList.add('darkMode')` breaks none of the three invariants. Add `.darkMode { background: var(--ink); color: var(--paper); }` in an app CSS file and the colours swap. That rule only reads tokens: it declares no `--x:`, uses no scheme API, and an unquoted CSS selector is never checked. The result forces a theme against the OS, which the spec forbids ('No app source … SHALL … name a scheme (`dark`, `light`, `theme…`) in a string literal'), and the guard stays green. The 'fine' fixtures only show that a camelCase *identifier* (`const darkMode`) is allowed; no fixture checks a camelCase *string*. Found by reading the regex; I couldn't run a probe test because running vitest needs approval in this session.
findings.suggestion: Inside string literals, match scheme words at camelCase and kebab boundaries too, for example `(?<![a-z])(dark|light|theme)(?![a-z])` without the `i` flag plus a separate check for capitalised `Dark|Light|Theme`. Or run a case-insensitive substring check on the string content and keep a short explicit allowlist. Add `"classList.add('darkMode')"` and `"el.className = 'isLight'"` to the `forced` fixtures.

findings.title: .dockerignore 'mirror' test compares text, but Docker anchors patterns at the root, so files git ignores in subfolders still reach the image
findings.evidence: The test only checks that each .gitignore line appears word for word in .dockerignore. Git matches unanchored patterns such as `uploads/`, `storage/`, `*.log`, `.env`, `.env.*` and `*.dump` at any depth. Docker (`filepath.Match` after Clean) matches them only at the context root; only `**/raw/` uses `**`. So `public/uploads/page.png` is ignored by git, hidden from `git status --porcelain` (smoke reports `dirty: false`), yet copied by `COPY . .` into the build, and Vite ships `public/` into dist. That workbook-content path is exactly the one NFR-4 rules out. The comment in .dockerignore and the round-7 commit claim that 'a clean commit is the whole build input'. The test passes while that is false for nested ignored files.
findings.suggestion: Write each unanchored .gitignore pattern as `**/<pattern>` in .dockerignore (e.g. `**/uploads/`, `**/*.log`, `**/.env`, `**/.env.*`). Make the test map gitignore semantics to Docker's: a pattern with no slash, or only a trailing one, must appear with a `**/` prefix. Or check that `git ls-files -oi --exclude-standard` lists nothing that `docker build` would send.

I confirmed this by reading `src/app/theme-source.test.ts:29-34`. I couldn't run the check because the command needed approval, so I traced it by hand. `withoutComments` uses plain regexes and doesn't know about strings.

1. The block-comment pattern `/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g` treats any `/*` as the start of a comment, including one inside a string. Take the input `import.meta.glob('./pages/*.tsx'); root.classList.add('dark'); /** Routes. */`. The match starts at the `/*` in `/*.tsx` and lazily runs to the first `*/`, which ends the JSDoc. Nothing earlier closes it: the `/**` only has `**` followed by a space. So `'dark'` is removed. What remains is `import.meta.glob('./pages` plus the trailing code. The quote is now unbalanced, and neither QUOTED_SCHEME nor TEMPLATE_SCHEME matches.

2. The line-comment pattern `(^|[^:\\'"\`])\/\/.*$` only skips `//` when it directly follows `:`, a backslash or a quote. In `el.className = 'a // dark';` the character before `//` is a space, so the rest of the line is dropped, `'dark'` included. Invariant 3 is then missed.

`themeViolations` runs on every app file (lines 93-97) and nothing else guards against this, so the gap is real. Its effect is limited: it is a false negative that only lowers coverage, and it needs a specific mix of string contents and a later comment. Minor severity is right.

I could not refute the finding. The mechanism it describes is real in this code.

**What the test checks.** In `src/test/container-config.test.ts:100-103`, the test only compares lines as plain strings. It checks that every non-negated `.gitignore` line also appears in `.dockerignore`. It does not account for the two tools reading the same pattern differently.

**How each tool reads the patterns.**
- Git matches a pattern with no slash in it (`*.log`, `.DS_Store`, `.env`, `.env.*`, `*.dump`) at any depth. A pattern that only has a trailing slash (`uploads/`, `storage/`, `pgdata/`, `backups/`, `node_modules/`) also matches a directory with that name at any depth.
- Docker's `.dockerignore` matching (moby patternmatcher) cleans each pattern and matches it against the path from the context root. So `*.log` matches only `x.log` at the root, and `uploads/` matches only `./uploads`. Only `**/raw/` matches at any depth, and `src/api/generated/` is anchored in both tools, so those two agree.

**Where nothing protects against it.** The Dockerfile at line 9 runs `COPY . .` and then `npm run build`. So these git-ignored files would enter the build context while `git status` stays clean:
- `src/.env`
- `public/foo.dump`
- `public/uploads/...`

Vite copies `public/` into `dist`, and the final image copies `dist`, so files from `public/` reach the shipped image. Both the `.dockerignore` comment and the test name claim the opposite: "the build context is exactly the tracked and untracked files git reports".

**Severity.** It only triggers if someone puts such a file in a subdirectory, so "minor" is right. The test does guarantee less than it says, though, and in the `public/` case the result is a real gap where ignored files can leak into the image (NFR-3/NFR-4 content such as uploads or dumps).

I could not refute this. The test at src/test/container-config.test.ts:100 only checks that each .gitignore line also appears, as the same text, in .dockerignore. The two files do contain the same lines: `*.log`, `.DS_Store`, `.env`, `.env.*`, `uploads/`, `storage/`, `pgdata/`, `backups/` and `*.dump` are all unanchored. Only `**/raw/` uses `**/`.

The two tools read these lines differently:
- **Git:** a pattern with no slash, or only a trailing slash, matches at any depth.
- **Docker:** .dockerignore patterns are matched with Go's filepath.Match against the path from the context root. Docker's docs give the example that `temp?` only excludes entries at the root. So `uploads/` excludes `./uploads` and nothing deeper, and `*.log` does not match `src/a.log`.

How it can actually happen:
1. The Dockerfile runs `COPY . .` and then `npm run build`.
2. Vite copies `public/` into `dist/`, and nginx serves `dist/`.
3. So a git-ignored `public/uploads/…`, `public/x.dump` or `public/.env.local` ends up in the image and is served.
4. `git status --porcelain` stays empty because the files are ignored, so the smoke evidence still records the commit as clean.

That breaks the guarantee the test's name and the .dockerignore comment promise: that a clean commit names exactly what the image was built from. It also undercuts the NFR-3/NFR-4 intent behind `uploads/` and `*.dump`.

What limits the impact: it only happens if a developer leaves ignored files in a subdirectory, mainly `public/`. Files under `src/` only reach the bundle if code imports them. That fits severity minor, so I'd keep it as is. The suggested fix (prefix those entries with `**/`, and have the test normalise patterns before comparing) is correct.
